title: The Mixtape of Maple Street
premise: When debate champion Theo Amberdale is paired with his estranged former best friend Priya Nair for a semester project documenting the neighborhood's fading Maple Street, they uncover a paper trail showing the city's 'voluntary relocation' plan is a rigged scheme to displace longtime residents — including Priya's grandmother and Theo's own mother. As they build a mixtape-style audio archive of residents' stories, their buried friendship fractures over how far they'll go: Theo wants to work through official channels, Priya wants to expose the corruption publicly, even if it means burning the mentor who helped them. At the final audition for a city youth showcase, they choose to play the residents' voices instead of their polished presentation, forcing an investigation that saves Maple Street — but only after a betrayal that nearly ends their partnership for good, and a hard-won reconciliation built on truth instead of history.
about_author: K. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former community organizer turned high school debate coach who writes stories about teenagers discovering that rules and justice aren't always the same thing. They live in a mid-sized rust-belt city where the neighborhood diners still argue about the last election.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. We meet Theo mid-debate-tournament, winning trophies while staying strategically invisible at school and silent at home, where his mother's eviction notice sits unopened on the kitchen table. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being excellent and unheard.

chapters.title: The Assignment Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ms. Okonkwo announces the semester project: pairs must document a 'living history' of a local place. Theo is paired with Priya Nair, his former best friend turned cold stranger since a falling-out two years ago. Emotional beat: dread disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: Maple Street, 7 A.M.
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya proposes Maple Street — her grandmother's block, slated for 'redevelopment.' She sets rigid terms for the partnership. Theo notices she's recording everything, even him. Emotional beat: prickly professionalism hiding old grief.

chapters.title: Mrs. Nair's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Interviewing Priya's grandmother, Theo hears the warmth of a neighborhood he never knew existed three blocks from his own house. Mrs. Nair mistakes them for friends again; neither corrects her. Emotional beat: nostalgia for a friendship that still aches.

chapters.title: The First Tape
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya plays Theo an old mixtape she made him in eighth grade, found while organizing her recordings — the last artifact of their friendship. They argue about why it ended; neither tells the whole truth. Emotional beat: the wound reopened, carefully.

chapters.title: Voluntary
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Digging through city council minutes for context, Theo notices the word 'voluntary' appearing in relocation offers to Maple Street residents — including his own mother, who signed something last month. Emotional beat: the first cold drop of suspicion.

chapters.title: The Appraiser's Math
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya cross-references property appraisals and finds every Maple Street offer is 40% below market — except one house, owned by a councilman's brother-in-law. She wants to go public; Theo urges caution. Emotional beat: the partnership's first real fault line.

chapters.title: Debate Club, After Hours
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's mentor, Coach Reyes — who also advises the council's youth board — warns him off 'conspiracy thinking' and offers a letter of recommendation if Theo stays focused on nationals. Emotional beat: flattered, steered, and uneasy.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knew
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A retired city clerk, Marcus Webb, confirms a pattern: appraisal contracts awarded to a firm owned by the councilman's donor. He gives them a box of records but begs them to be careful. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of evidence.

chapters.title: The Mixtape Method
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo proposes their project format: a 'mixtape' of Maple Street voices — side A the neighborhood's past, side B its fight to survive. For one afternoon, working on it feels like being friends again. Emotional beat: cautious joy, the old rhythm returning.

chapters.title: Eviction Week
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The first family is evicted; Priya films it and posts a raw clip that goes local-viral. Theo is furious she acted without him; she says he'd have talked her out of it. He would have. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the honesty neither can deny.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Coach Reyes submits Theo's nationals paperwork — and Theo realizes the coach's youth-board position is funded by the developer's foundation. Confronted, Reyes admits the connection but insists he's protecting Theo's future. Emotional beat: a mentor's fall, in slow motion.

chapters.title: Side A / Side B
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They finish the mixtape: side A is love letters to Maple Street; side B is the corruption, narrated by residents themselves. Theo wants to submit the safe version to the city showcase; Priya wants side B. Emotional beat: the argument that decides everything.

chapters.title: The Deal
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's mother receives a final offer: sign now or lose the house by spring. She asks Theo, the family's golden child, what he thinks. He realizes staying quiet has been his way of choosing. Emotional beat: the cost of neutrality, finally priced.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Someone leaks that Priya and Theo are 'investigating' — her grandmother's rent doubles overnight as retaliation, and the records box goes missing from Marcus's apartment. Priya suspects Theo told Coach Reyes. Emotional beat: trust shattered at the worst moment.

chapters.title: What Theo Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo didn't leak anything — but he did show Reyes the appraisal numbers weeks ago, thinking he was asking for guidance. He confesses to Priya. She walks. Emotional beat: guilt without excuse, the friendship at zero.

chapters.title: Solo Nationals
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo competes at the debate national qualifier and wins — using an argument built from Maple Street testimony, then abandoning his prepared case to speak the truth on stage. He loses the round. He doesn't care. Emotional beat: choosing justice over winning, at last.

chapters.title: The Audition List
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya learns their city youth showcase audition — the biggest platform in town, livestreamed — is the deadline Ms. Okonkwo set for the project. She drafts a solo version of side B. Then she listens to side A and hears how much of it is Theo. Emotional beat: pride versus the missing half.

chapters.title: Two Chairs, One Microphone
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo shows up at Priya's door with the recovered records — Marcus hid them, and Reyes, quietly resigning, gave Theo the donor ledger. No speeches; just the mixtape playing between them. They rebuild the audition as a duo. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On stage, they abandon the approved presentation and play the residents' voices — evictions, appraisals, Mrs. Nair's kitchen — ending with the councilman's own recorded promises. The livestream clips spread before they leave the building. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into power.

chapters.title: Investigation, Spring
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The state opens an inquiry; the appraisal contracts are voided and the councilman resigns. Maple Street's relocation plan is suspended pending review. Mrs. Nair's rent freezes; Theo's mother tears up the offer. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: Side C
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, closing. Summer on Maple Street: the block party, Ms. Okonkwo giving them an A with a note that says 'finally, the truth,' and Theo and Priya recording a side C — not a document, just two friends talking. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen and kept.
